Confidence Intervals for an amerasfit Object

confint.Rd

Computes confidence or credible intervals for the parameters of a fitted amerasfit object and returns the interval bounds. The fitted object is not amended. Use add_confint to attach intervals and any available profile diagnostics to an amerasfit object for inclusion in summary() output and recording of confidence-interval timing.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'amerasfit'
confint(object, parm="dose", level=0.95,
        type=c("proflik","percentile"), maxit.profCI=20,
        tol.profCI=1e-2, data=NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model object of class amerasfit, as returned by ameras.

parm

Either "dose" to compute profile likelihood intervals for dose-related parameters only, "all" for all parameters, or a character vector of parameter names. Only used when type = "proflik". Defaults to "dose" because profile likelihood intervals can be computationally intensive.

level

Confidence level, as a single number between zero and one. Defaults to 0.95.

type

Interval type. For RC, ERC, and MCML, use "wald.orig", "wald.transformed", or "proflik". For FMA and BMA, use "percentile" or "hpd". When both groups of methods are present, supply one type for each group.

maxit.profCI

Maximum number of root-finding iterations for profile likelihood intervals. Defaults to 20.

tol.profCI

Root-finding tolerance for profile likelihood intervals. Defaults to 1e-2.

data

Original fitting data. Required for profile likelihood intervals when the model was fitted with keep.data = FALSE.

...

Additional arguments, currently unused. To attach intervals to a fitted object or control printed output, use add_confint.

Value

For an object containing one fitted method, a numeric matrix with parameters in rows and the lower and upper confidence limits in two percentage-labelled columns. For an object containing multiple fitted methods, a named list of such matrices, one per method.

Details

For RC, ERC, and MCML, Wald intervals on the original parameter scale use the delta-method variance-covariance matrix. Wald intervals on the transformed scale are computed in the optimization parametrization and then back-transformed. More specifically, when \(\boldsymbol\theta = h(\boldsymbol\eta)\), transformed-scale intervals apply \(h\) to the endpoints on the \(\boldsymbol\eta\) scale, whereas original-scale intervals use the covariance matrix obtained from \(J H^{-1} J^T\), where \(J\) is the transformation Jacobian and \(H\) is the optimization Hessian. Profile likelihood intervals repeatedly re-evaluate the likelihood and can therefore be substantially more expensive.

For FMA and BMA, percentile intervals use equal-tailed sample quantiles and HPD intervals use HPDinterval.

Profile likelihood diagnostics such as boundary p-values and iteration counts are not included in the returned matrices. Use add_confint to store these diagnostics in the method-specific CI components of a fitted object.

The requested intervals are always computed, even if object already contains attached intervals. The input object is left unchanged. If a profile likelihood bound cannot be reliably bracketed or solved, that bound is returned as NA with a diagnostic warning.

When a model was fitted with keep.data = FALSE, the original data must be supplied through data for profile likelihood intervals. The missing-value policy used during fitting is reapplied before likelihood evaluation. Wald and sample-based intervals do not require the original data. For models with formula effect modifiers, subgroup-specific profile intervals can be obtained by fitting subgroup-specific dose coefficients with modifier = ~ 0 + M or modifier = ~ M - 1.

See also

add_confint for attaching intervals and diagnostics to a fit, ameras for model fitting, summary for fit summaries, and confint for the generic function.

Examples

fit <- ameras(
  Y.binomial ~ dose(V1:V3, model = "ERR"),
  data = ameras_simulated,
  family = "binomial",
  methods = "RC"
)
#> Fitting RC

## A two-column matrix of Wald interval bounds
confint(fit, type = "wald.orig")
#>                  2.5 %     97.5 %
#> (Intercept) -1.0297063 -0.7404073
#> dose         0.5338981  1.0748159

## Profile likelihood intervals are slower

confint(fit, type = "proflik", parm = "dose")
#> Obtaining profile likelihood CI for dose
#>          2.5 %   97.5 %
#> dose 0.5663534 1.115075
